# Warm MessageChannel continuation experiment

2026-09-13. Design only; no runtime/test edits or execution, agent delegation, commits or publication. Implementer handoff: **Luna xhigh → fresh Astra medium review → Root-owned measured comparison and qualification**. User-requested model workflow overrides the repository's default Sol workflow.

## Baseline and one change

Start at published adapter 0.5.1, `cced684beb84f2152cd237beeecd40e4d9a68ab6`, clean `/tmp/miso-task-yield-adapter` (dependencies installed). Engine 0.2.4, codec 0.1.1, Effect 4.0.0-rc.112 remain fixed. Read this repository's AGENTS.md. This plan carries forward [selection](next-path-selection.md), [zero gate adjudication](zero-gate-adjudication.md), [zero decision](zero-yield-decision.md) and [packed decision](packed-reads-decision.md). Neither shelved candidate is included.

Change only how warm `verifyMarker` zero checkpoints resume: a private reused MessageChannel task replaces the explicit `Effect.yieldNow` at the unchanged 64 KiB boundary, including each nonempty gap's final partial/full block. Add an optional private yield Effect to `hashZeros`, defaulting to its existing yield, and supply it from the two warm call sites. Keep the shared helper and cold calls. No new public exports/configuration, scheduler service override, global channel/registry, queue framework, priority policy, per-block channel construction, backend change or app UI change. Defer worker design entirely. No engine/audio/codec/feed/pump/format/admission/metadata/progress-policy edits.

Preserve exact admitted Blob descriptor identity, full ordered canonical BLAKE3/byte verification before ready, raw hash-update and progress boundaries, observer isolation and observer-triggered cancellation. Keep interval-local 512 KiB reads, source order/width, and cold 128 KiB span and current yield behavior. Ghost accounting stays 845 payload reads, 249,323,400 active bytes, 297,980,304 canonical hashed bytes, eight accepted stems, no warm resolver/FLAC requests. The existing arithmetic predicts 1,010 warm zero checkpoints; do not label that number an executed observation without tracing it.

## Minimal resource and lifecycle contract

A small private closure owned by an inner Effect scope in `verifyMarker` is sufficient. Acquire a logical resource and register its finalizer before it can allocate native ports; allocate one channel lazily on the first actual warm zero yield, reuse it until verification exits. All-active verification allocates none. The inner scope must finish before `verifyMarker` returns to either `openSource` or warm `installSource`, hence before source-ready and before the outer identity-lock release. Do not move resource ownership to the store/session or change their existing close implementation.

The resource needs only optional ports, a closed flag and at most one pending continuation/cleanup slot. Install one message handler; post a trivial notification, not PCM. A yield uses `Effect.callback`, checks the operation signal before registering and after listener installation, records its pending continuation before posting, and suspends until delivery. Clear the slot and remove that wait's abort listener **before** resuming, because Effect can execute the next yield synchronously within the resume callback. Completion is once-only. Reject an impossible overlapping wait rather than overwriting it. No queue or unbounded history is needed.

The pending wait listens to the operation signal (which already combines caller and store close). Abort must clear/detach and resume `SparseCancelledError` immediately without waiting for port delivery. Effect callback interruption cleanup also detaches/invalidates the pending wait; verifier finalization closes the resource. No extra operation-wide abort wiring is needed when idle: existing signal checks guard subsequent work. A cancelled verifier never reuses its channel; late callbacks must see closed/no-pending state and do nothing, including after retry creates a new resource. On final-byte observer abort, the new yield must reject before digest/readiness; preserve existing post-terminal-progress checks too.

Cleanup is idempotent: invalidate the slot first, detach handler/listeners, attempt both port closes even if one throws, clear references. On success cleanup finishes before returning a descriptor; on failure/abort it finishes before identity-lock release. Unexpected construction/handler-registration/post failures must become an existing typed boundary failure, settle any installed wait and close any acquired ports, never hang or silently claim fast-path success. Close errors must be surfaced through existing Effect/public cause mapping (no new public error codes), prevent source-ready, and never skip the second close; use the existing Effect finalization style rather than a custom recovery framework. Normal platform close is synchronous; injected close failure can prove both close attempts and rejection, not guarantee a hostile port physically closed. Cleanup must not depend on another message/timer.

Only absent/non-callable `globalThis.MessageChannel` uses the old `Effect.yieldNow` fallback. Do not add alternate scheduler APIs or silently fall back after a runtime post failure. Fallback keeps cancellation checks/cadence; mark that arm as fallback in diagnostic evidence, never as the candidate fast path. Preserve current configured read deadlines/refusal semantics; do not add a task timeout or adjust the Blob read path.

## Effect boundary checked in installed source

`node_modules/effect/src/internal/effect.ts:1102` (`callbackOptions`) records an asynchronous suspension and invokes `fiber.evaluate(effect)` directly from a later callback. `evaluate` at line 599 immediately enters `runLoop`; it does not unconditionally dispatch a timer first. `yieldNowWith` at line 982 instead calls the current dispatcher. `Scheduler.ts:84` selects `setImmediate` when present, otherwise `setTimeout(0)`. Automatic `shouldYield` handling remains at `effect.ts:643–651`; leave it and all runtime settings alone. Thus the proposed resume avoids an *added explicit* timer yield; it does not guarantee zero automatic yields, fairness, immediate execution or painting.

Root needs one small separate executed browser diagnostic against the reviewed packed candidate: a bounded multi-gap fixture and temporary instrumentation around actual warm checkpoints/port callbacks. Record registration returning before delivery, callback entry, the next warm continuation executing during resume, checkpoint totals, and any intervening automatic scheduler dispatch. A handler-active marker around `resume` plus a checkpoint marker is enough to show the direct boundary; do not build a general scheduler tracer or instrument every Ghost task. Retain instrumentation diff, packed artifact identity and small raw event log; normal timing uses the uninstrumented package. If the continuation always returns through a timer, investigate before timing: the central candidate boundary has not been demonstrated. This diagnostic establishes path behavior, not timer-clamp causation.

## Focused implementation/review evidence

Reuse existing sparse fixtures and independent digest oracles, adding only cases that exercise the changed seam. A small fake MessageChannel in tests may hold/deliver messages and count live ports/listeners; no production public seam or generalized task simulator.

- One compact integrity/cadence fixture group: all-active/no-channel, silent/mixed and exact/adjacent frame-aligned 64 KiB gaps with a partial tail. Independent canonical byte/digest oracle; compare raw updates/progress and yield counts with baseline; include tamper rejection. Existing cold fixture must retain its original cadence. Run both warm public entry paths through existing coverage rather than duplicating all combinations.
- One held-message lifecycle group: external abort and store close settle without delivering it, no readiness or successful terminal event, ports/listeners released before lock release; deliver stale callbacks afterward, then retry successfully. Include final-zero-progress observer abort and throwing-observer isolation using existing fixtures. Check reuse across gaps, single pending wait, and no residual resources across a few reopen cycles.
- One bounded failure/fallback group: absent capability uses old yields and completes correctly; construction/post failure rejects with cleanup; a close fault still attempts both closes and blocks readiness. These are representative ownership edges, not an exhaustive event-order matrix.

Run repository `npm run check` (includes format/build/lint/typecheck/decoder/full tests/package checks); avoid repeating all checks after unchanged artifacts. Fresh Astra reviews scope, cancellation/finalizer ordering, callback reentrancy and exact identity/byte/cadence preservation, and runs appropriate focused tests. Root freezes source/test/package/app manifest hashes before comparing. Tests or source inspection alone do not qualify browser performance.

The known stalled-Blob abort limitation remains separately disclosed: published control and previous candidate waited for configured read deadline and returned `stem.read_deadline` rather than prompt `stem.cancelled` while physical read was withheld. Do not fix it here or call it a passing prompt-abort case. Keep the recorded reproducer/identities; no unrelated repeated matrix. New failures at the changed task-yield boundary remain blocking.

## Frozen paired decision, owned by Root

A = published 0.5.1; B = reviewed private candidate. Same real Chromium/device, Ghost corpus/cache, app, width eight, source order, observers, navigation/GC procedure and one unmeasured warm prime per arm. First block exactly five pairs **AB, BA, AB, BA, AB**. Separate diagnostics and memory from timing. Preserve every row, failure and artifact/harness identity; report ready/ingest values, paired deltas and arm ranges, not a five-sample p95.

For paired savings `d = A.ready − B.ready`, use `D = median(d)`, `M = median(abs(d − D))`, `C = median(A.ready)`, `T = max(10 ms, 0.01*C, 2*M)`. First block passes timing only if at least 4/5 deltas are strictly positive and `D > T` (equality fails). All independent integrity/resource/responsiveness gates must also pass for acceptance.

Predeclare the sole extension now: only if 4/5 or more are faster and `0.8*T <= D <= T`, with `D > max(10 ms, 0.01*C)`, may Root collect one additional five-pair block **BA, AB, BA, AB, BA**. Otherwise a failing first block is shelved, including clear null/regression. This defines consequential borderline before seeing results. On extension decide once over all ten rows: at least 8/10 strictly faster and pooled `D > max(10 ms, 0.01*C, 2*M)`, recomputing all quantities; even medians average the central values. Report both blocks and pooled result. No third block, favorable-row removal, arm-median substitution or alternative scheduling arm. Objectively invalid infrastructure rows remain recorded with reason; inability to obtain the declared valid pairs is inconclusive, not permission to extend indefinitely. Integrity/cancellation failures are not removable slow observations. This is a descriptive screen with a disclosed interim look, not a statistical confidence claim.

## Independent browser, memory and adoption gates

Reuse width-one/eight CPU fairness fixtures on uninstrumented arms: no candidate-created task over 50 ms, heartbeat lateness ≤50 ms, external CPU abort-to-rejection ≤100 ms with cancellation/no-ready and successful retry. One separate matched real-app warm Ghost diagnostic per arm observes 10 ms heartbeat, long tasks and DOM progress at rAF opportunities: no new verifier task over 50 ms, heartbeat p95 increase ≤10 ms, and ≤250 ms gaps in observed DOM progress while bytes advance. Record first/final progress and rAF gaps; identify unrelated startup tasks rather than attributing all long tasks to verification. A candidate-specific freeze blocks acceptance. **These DOM/rAF measurements replace screenshot/paint proof under the prior adjudication. They show committed progress and rendering opportunities, not pixels painted. No screenshot/video machinery.**

Three separate sampled memory runs per arm using the existing sampler: preserve one ≤512 KiB payload buffer per verifier (≤4 MiB at width eight), shared 64 KiB zeros, bounded metadata and only two ports/one pending slot per verifier that needs gaps. Record all peaks and resource cleanup/reopen observations. Unexplained median peak rise greater than `max(4 MiB, 5% of control)` blocks acceptance; do not call excluded browser/OPFS/worker memory zero or introduce a new memory framework.

Root runs existing packed fresh-consumer/browser and actual OPFS lanes for a viable candidate, plus required repository checks and publish dry-run; app adoption also requires the app's lint/typecheck/test/build. Reuse existing harnesses, not a new corpus/browser matrix. Missing lanes are explicit qualification blockers, never passes. Physical Safari/iPad correctness/performance remains unqualified without actual target evidence; this does not prevent clearly labeled Chromium selection. No publication/adoption is authorized by this design handoff. If the candidate loses, archive the exact diff/results and stop; no stacked microchanges or worker implementation. Describe an accepted result only as a measured warm task-yield path improvement on the measured target, never proof of timer clamping, portable performance or sub-second ready.
